entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Phaedrus the Epicurean (phaedrus-the-epicurean) was a prominent Epicurean philosopher and head of the Epicurean school in Athens from around 75 BC until his death in 69 or 70 BC. He was a contemporary of Cicero, with whom he renewed his acquaintance in Rome.

Phaedrus was a leading figure of the Epicurean school, known for his philosophical writings and teachings. He was also a friend of Velleius, with whom Cicero was acquainted.

Phaedrus' legacy continued through his successors, who carried on his philosophical ideas and spread them throughout the ancient world.

His impact on the development of Epicureanism was profound, shaping the school's philosophical stance and influencing its adherents.

The exact date of Phaedrus' birth is unknown, but his significance in the history of Epicureanism is undeniable.
